task_name: Milepost Driving Academy - Scenario clip training library
client_brief:
Milepost is starting with two scenarios rather than the whole library. If these two land with learners and with the parents watching over their shoulder, we will commission the rest on the same pattern.

Our learners watch on a phone with the sound off, so nothing is spoken in these clips. No narration, no voice over, no synthetic instructor. The instruction goes on screen, word for word from the approved copy, one step at a time, in the order the copy gives, and the clips run silent. Every clip, the upright example included, also carries its scenario number, which is that scenario's place in the running order of the approved copy.

Deliverables
1. Right turns explainer: 1 named export, 1920 by 1080, 12 to 15 seconds, silent. All five steps from the Right turns row on screen in order, then the callout for that row.
2. Four-way stops explainer: 1 named export, 1920 by 1080, 10 to 12 seconds, silent. All four steps from the Four-way stops row on screen in order, then the callout for that row, and our simplified stop sign shape, recovered from the wall sheet, shown at least once.
3. Vertical lane changes example: 1 named export, 1080 by 1920, 6 to 9 seconds, silent. The scenario number, the scenario title and the callout only, with no steps, so we can see how the road reads upright on a phone before we commit the rest of the library to that format.

Show the manoeuvre, do not imply it. A learner should be able to see the car do the thing the step describes. If a step is not visible in the footage we have given you, say so in the delivery manifest rather than cutting unrelated road shots together until the manoeuvre looks finished.

Two notes on the source. The two four way stop takes are the same junction filmed on two passes in different lanes, so please do not present them as two different junctions. Road context has to stay readable in the upright example: if the lane line leaves the frame, the example teaches nothing.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.
Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, a still montage PDF or an editing log. Audio expectations are stated on each film. No film in this commission carries speech or music: every clip is delivered silent, with the instruction set on screen.
Authored animation can exceed the duration of still source images. Live action edits require adequate distinct footage; looping a short clip is not a substitute for missing coverage.
Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.typography: Milepost runs a four step scale. Step 01, display, is Baskerville Display PT Regular at 72 px on 80 px leading with tracking of minus 10 units for the scenario title, and the scenario number sets in the same face at three times that size, 216 px, in Signal Green with a 3 px Caution Amber rule directly beneath it. The vertical cutdown title runs 64 px on 72 px, and the school name is the only other Baskerville setting, in Bold. Step 02, subheading, is Inter Semibold at 56 px on 64 px with tracking of minus 5 units for callouts, because Baskerville is reserved for the school name and scenario titles. Step 03, body, is Inter Regular at 44 px on 58 px, tracking 0, to a maximum of 65 characters. Step 04, fine print, is Inter Regular at 32 px on 42 px with tracking of plus 20 units for captions and the accreditation line. Inter carries tabular lining figures at every size, the printed guide sets body at 11 pt on 16 pt, and a step is never set in italic or caps.
brand_identity.voice: Calm, instructive, reassuring. One idea at a time, numbered where it helps, no slang and no drama. Speaks plainly to a beginner and to the parent reading over their shoulder.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Everything a learner currently sees from us dates to 2019 and looks it. The printer holds the press file for the guide, but the source files for our simplified sign shapes are gone: they only survive as a photograph of a sheet our first designer printed and taped to the wall, so those glyphs have to be recovered from that. No brand typeface was ever locked, so the type system is open for you to set to our legibility standard.
brand_identity.values: Certainty over style. A learner and a parent must always be sure what they are looking at. Nothing stylised, nothing that reads as styling over substance, consistency that shows the school is careful.

palette_rules.distribution: Route White is the only ground: the scenario number, title, steps and callout sit on a solid Route White card or panel, never directly on road footage, as milepost_guide_2019.pdf keeps its type off the photograph. On Route White, the scenario number and scenario title are Signal Green, and step lines, the callout and captions are Slate Text, as on milepost_guide_2019.pdf. Caution Amber is for thin rules only and Sky Grey for a footer or accreditation line and hairlines only; together they take no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area and are never a ground, a panel, step text or callout text.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity, once a card or panel is fully on screen. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow, glow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over the road footage: text sits on a solid Route White card or panel.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, panels, rules or glyphs, so no red stop sign glyph, and no gradient, glow, outline, drop shadow or metallic effect on any type, panel, rule or glyph: nothing is stylised.
palette_rules.photography: Road footage and road stills keep their own filmed colour and are never tinted or graded toward the palette. The warm low-sun cast of milepost_road_still_01.jpg and milepost_road_still_02.jpg is not pushed toward Caution Amber, the cool fog of milepost_road_still_03.jpg and milepost_road_still_04.jpg is not pushed toward Sky Grey, and the painted road markings in every take keep the colours they were filmed in.
